fields.meta_description: Build a check in form that collects what you need before someone arrives and tells the right person when an answer needs action. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Check in Form That Flags Who Needs Attention
fields.hero_description: Build a check in form that flags the answers that need follow-up and saves every check-in to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What a Check in Form Should Do at the Door
fields.features_subheading: A sheet collects names. These parts get the news to whoever has to act, in time.
fields.feature_1:
Questions that follow each answer

Show the allergy field only when a parent ticks yes, or ask for a plate number only when a guest is driving. Nobody has to scroll past questions that do not apply to them.
fields.feature_2:
Alerts on the answers you care about

Pick the answers that need someone to act: a late arrival, a low rating, a missing ID. The form sends the owner a Slack message or an email with the full check-in attached.
fields.feature_3:
Check in ahead or at the door

Send the link the day before so guests answer at home, or run the same form on a kiosk tablet at the entrance. Both routes write to one record, and nobody types it twice.
fields.feature_4:
ID photos and files on the record

Ask for a photo of a driver's license, a signed waiver, or a vaccination card. Each upload stays on its own check-in, where the desk opens it without searching an inbox.
fields.feature_5:
A roster for every room and date

Every check-in becomes a row in a database you own. Filter by room, shift, or date, sort the flagged entries to the top, and export the rows to a spreadsheet when you need them.
fields.feature_6:
The full source code is yours

Export the code behind your check-in app to your GitHub repository on paid plans. A developer can host it on your own servers or link it to the front desk or school system you run.

fields.usecase_heading: Where a Check-In Needs Someone to Act
fields.tab_content_1:
Arriving at 11:40 PM, after the desk has closed

Harbor Street Inn has 12 rooms and a front desk that closes at 10 PM. Guests get the online check-in the day before and enter their arrival time, an ID photo, a parking plate, and any requests. Nora Keller says 11:40 PM. Night manager Luis Ortiz gets a Slack message naming Room 7 and her plate.
fields.tab_content_2:
Two students who asked to talk reach the counselor

Advisory at Linden Middle starts at 7:50 with a two-question check-in on each school laptop. Students rate their morning on a 1 to 5 scale and can tick a box that asks to talk with an adult. All 26 answered today. Two of them picked a 1 or ticked the box, and counselor Ms. Abara has both names before first period at 8:10.
fields.tab_content_3:
A peanut allergy sits above all 11 names

Sunday mornings at Grace Hill Church, parents check their children in at a kiosk before the 9:30 service. Each check-in records the child's room and any allergy a parent has entered. Room leader Carmen Diaz opens the 3-year-olds roster on her tablet and sees 11 children, with Theo Marsh's peanut allergy pinned first.
fields.tab_content_4:
Workload 5 on two Fridays in a row

Every Friday at 3 PM, nine support reps at Fernway answer a short check-in: a workload rating out of 5 and one line on what is blocking them. Manager Owen Pratt reads the summary on Monday morning. Priya Shah rated her workload 5 this week and last, and her row leads it, ahead of the other eight.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Check in Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to create a check in form that gathers what you need on arrival and alerts the right person, then build it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Keep it to what you act on
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Decide who hears about each reply
fields.howto_step_1_des: Decide when people check in: the day before arrival, at the door, or at a set time each week. Schools often run student check-ins during advisory or a morning meeting, when every student is already at a screen.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Ask only for details that change what someone does next. A guest's expected time tells the night manager whether to wait up. A favorite color tells nobody anything. Four or five questions is plenty for most check-ins, and people finish them.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Pair each reply that needs follow-up with one named person. A late arrival goes to the night manager; an allergy goes to the room leader. Children's check-in systems print allergies on name tags for that reason. Plan where yours will appear.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Guests do best on their own phone with a link sent the day before. Parents and visitors use a tablet by the entrance. Students use the laptops they already have. Plan the layout for the smallest of those screens.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Put the questions into the prompt, along with which replies need follow-up and who hears about each one. Emergent builds the form, its logic, and the database behind it. Change any part later by prompting again, without starting over.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Ask for the view the person on duty will open: tonight's arrivals for the desk, one room's children for a volunteer, flagged rows first for a manager. Check that it reads clearly on the device they carry.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Check in as a guest with a reply that should trigger an alert, such as a time after closing. Confirm the message reaches the night manager with the details attached. Then open the roster and find the test entry at the top.

plan.angle: The top 10 is a shelf of templates: Jotform and Cognito Forms galleries, a Formuiz check-in and check-out sheet, 123FormBuilder's hotel confirmation, a SurveyJS code sample, a Pinterest board of hotel cards, a published Microsoft Forms page, Panorama's student check-in prompts and a Planning Center help article. They agree a check-in is a short form, and they stop at the answers. A check-in exists so somebody acts on arrival: the night manager who needs to know a guest lands after the desk closes, the counselor who should see one student before first period, the room leader who must know about a peanut allergy. This page treats the form as that signal, with four settings that check in differently (guests before arrival, students each morning, children at a Sunday service, a team every Friday) and leaves visitor sign-in, sign-out and registration to their own pages.
tab_stories: A 12-room inn sends every guest an online check-in the day before arrival, and one couple landing at 11:40 PM, after the desk closes at 10 PM, puts the night manager on notice with their parking plate and room.
A seventh-grade advisory answers a two-question morning check-in on Chromebooks, and the two students out of 26 who pick a 1 or ask to talk reach the school counselor's list before first period.
Parents check their children in at a church kiosk before the 9:30 service, and the leader of the 3-year-olds room sees 11 names with one peanut allergy marked at the top of her roster.
A support manager's nine reports answer a Friday check-in on workload, wins and blockers, and the Monday summary puts the one rep rating workload 5 two weeks running first on his list.
